Cc: ops@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment fallback & version-pin guarantee request

Hi Jonas,

Quick one from our infra and procurement teams as we prepare the integration POC next week. We need a written confirmation that during any staged deployment (canary / A–B) Redwood can:  

- Automatically fail back traffic to the previously-stable model variant if latency or error spikes exceed agreed thresholds.
- Allow us to request an immediate pin to the previous model/version for a specified window (we typically ask for 24–72 hours) while we triage.

Can you also outline the monitoring/telemetry you’ll provide and whether this requires an SLA amendment (Procurement wants to know if we need a signed addendum before the POC). Attached is a short list of the telemetry fields we’ll need.

Thanks — can we hop on a 30-minute call this afternoon to align?

— Samantha

Proposed internal plan:
- Provide an explicit canary policy we can commit to for the POC: small traffic slice, watch window, automated fallback threshold, and a documented version-lock process initiated by the customer via Console + Support escalation.

Would like to respond to Samantha with a concrete checklist and a proposed amendment draft by EOD.

— Jonas

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Deployment fallback & version-pin guarantee request

Jonas — technical details below we can operationally guarantee for the POC without backend changes: 

Canary / A–B policy (baseline for POC):
- Traffic slice: 5% production traffic to canary cohort (configurable).
- Watch window: 10 minutes rolling; evaluation window 2–5 minutes within that.
- Failure triggers (examples we can instrument now):
  - Request error rate spike: +1.5x baseline over rolling 5m window.
  - Latency degradation: 95th percentile increases by > 250ms relative to baseline for 2 consecutive evaluation windows.
  - Regression in key quality signals (if applicable) — optional and depends on Acme-provided evals.
- Automatic fallback behavior:
  - If any trigger fires, traffic is automatically routed back to the last-stable variant within 60–90s.
  - We keep the canary variant in read-only for diagnostics; requests are not sent to the canary after failover.
- Version lock (customer-initiated):
  - Console option + Support API to pin a version for 24/48/72 hour windows. Pinning stops all rollout automation until unlocked.
  - Pin requests generate an audit event and require a single Support ACK for enterprise customers.

Telemetry and evidence we will provide:
- Per-variant latency percentiles, error rates, request volume, and autoscaling events (1s granularity for the canary window).
- Rollout actions (timestamped): start, traffic % changes, failover, pin/unpin events.
- Downloadable JSON/CSV snapshot of the watch window on demand.

Operational caveats:
- Automatic fallback is best-effort for POC and relies on console-configured thresholds. For a contractual SLA amendment (credits tied to miss), we’ll need Legal to sign a short addendum that defines the thresholds and credits.

Attaching the internal canary playbook and a sample telemetry snapshot.

— Marcus
Principle Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 14:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Deployment fallback & version-pin guarantee request

Samantha — thanks for raising this and for the specificity. We can support Acme’s request for the POC with the following commitment and conditions: 

Commitment (POC window only):
- Redwood will enable a canary deployment pattern with automatic failback to the last-stable variant when configured thresholds (error-rate or latency regressions) are met, as described in the attached playbook.
- Customers may request a version pin (24/48/72 hours) via the Console; Support will acknowledge and create an audit record.

Conditions / required items:
- The guarantee for automatic fallback during the POC is an operational commitment and not a permanent change to the standard SLA. If you want credits tied to rollout failures, we will need a signed addendum.
- The POC carve-out will be limited to the integration period (dates to be confirmed on the call).
- We will provide the per-rollout telemetry snapshots and a weekly summary while the POC is running.

Next steps:
1) I’ve attached a one-page amendment draft (acme_sla_amendment_draft.docx) that defines thresholds and the limited credit cap; if Procurement is OK, we can DocuSign it for the POC.
2) Marcus has provided the telemetry and playbook. Monica will share Console steps for pinning in a separate note.
3) Jonas — please schedule the 30-min alignment. Samantha — does 4:00pm PT work?

— Laura
Head of Sales (Redwood Inference)
[attachment: acme_sla_amendment_draft.docx]

- Can you confirm the exact console path for initiating a pin (and whether an API call is available for automating it)?
- For the automatic fallback, is the 60–90s rollback window a hard maximum or best-effort? Procurement wants to know whether they should model the P0 impact window as up to 2 minutes.

If you can include the Console steps and sample API call in the meeting notes, we’ll be able to sign the amendment during the POC start.

Looking forward — Samantha
Head of Platform, Acme Health
